description:
Hi everyone! I’m Mahmoud Hammam, a Mechatronics Engineering student passionate about embedded systems, robotics, and hardware-software integration.

My hands-on background covers SolidWorks CAD design, embedded prototyping (Arduino, STM32, ESP32) and C++ / Python. I’ve led and built end-to-end hardware projects—ranging from CNC machines and line followers combined with active leadership in student technical activities and project coordination.

Let’s team up and win!
summary: Project helix is a health monitoring locally hosted software, which brings imagination into reality through visualizing human anatomy into a 3D model, allowing problem discovery with high precision, and providing full logs of astronaut medical history for cross examination and pattern recognition, the software is connected to a wearable device which can detect abnormalities and give live feedback.
details:
The monitoring app first gives the user a login interface and can only log in as a CDR (one watch and one user per astronaut). After logging in, the user sees a 3d human model with detailed anatomical analysis and each time he clicks on a part of that 3d model it opens up a card which shows data. On the right there is an api key used from nasa which is the nasa space weather and radiation. All the readings are demonstrated/simulated except the SpO2, BPM , and blood pressure which will be transmitted by the microcontroller through the sensors. And there will be real actual nasa data for the space radiation

Vision: Turn imagination into reality which gives smooth interaction and ease of understanding data.

Goal: to actually solve problems and look for other real sensors and help everyone analyze their own medical condition and not only for astronauts.

There are three modes (anatomy)

Modes include 4000 different names of real anatomy

First mode: Skeleton.

Only sees the skeleton of the body

Second mode: Muscles.

Only sees the muscles of the body.

Third mode: Combined.

Sees the skeleton and the muscles combined
projectRefs: Source model for the human body
